answer: Latency-Bid Admission Curve. Each new identity must submit a bid that sets its transaction priority; the protocol prices admission as a convex function of identities created per epoch, so marginal cost rises steeply. An attacker registering many agents faces accelerating fees, like a juniper spreading where each new root costs more. Legitimate low-volume agents pay little. The curve steepens past a dune threshold of registrations per cycle. Under burst load a gale of signups forces the attacker's per-identity spend far above honest operators' returns, making mass fabrication unprofitable.
